page.overview:
Who is Edgar Barth?

(born 26 January 1917 and died 20 May 1965) was a German racing driver who participated in Formula One during the 1950s and 1960s. He also had great success racing sports cars and Formula 2.

After starting his racing career on motorcycles, he began racing sportscars in East Germany in 1951. By 1952, he had started racing in East German Formula 2 with the factory Eisenacher Motorenwerk (EMW) team, winning the championship in 1952 and 1953.

With this success, he was allowed to race with EMW outside of East Germany in 1953. He made his Formula One debut in the non-championship 1953 Internationales ADAC Eifelrennen, finishing in fifth position. He later drove in the non-championship 1953 Avusrennen, although he retired early due to a clutch failure. He participated in his first championship race at the 1953 German Grand Prix, but again retired due to a mechanical issue.

He continued racing in Formula 2 and a variety of other motorsports throughout 1954, 1955, and 1956. Political issues prevented him from racing in West Germany for much of that time. Despite this, he caught the attention of while racing in France and was offered a factory drive with the team at the Nürburgring. Despite disapproval from the East German authorities, he participated in the event anyway.
